question: What is meant by consent and free consent? Briefly explain the factors that take away the freedom of consent under the Indian Contract Act, 1872.

points.label: Consent and free consent
points.description: Consent means two or more persons agreeing on the same thing in the same sense; consent is free when it is not caused by coercion, undue influence, fraud, misrepresentation or mistake.

points.label: Coercion
points.description: Committing or threatening any act forbidden by the Indian Penal Code (now the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita), or unlawfully detaining or threatening to detain property, to make a person enter into an agreement.

points.label: Undue influence
points.description: Where one party is in a position to dominate the will of the other (for example, real or apparent authority, a fiduciary relation, or mental distress of the other) and uses that position to gain an unfair advantage.

points.label: Fraud and misrepresentation
points.description: Fraud is a false statement or active concealment made knowingly with intent to deceive; misrepresentation is an untrue statement made innocently, believing it to be true. Both make the contract voidable at the option of the deceived party.

points.label: Mistake and effect
points.description: A bilateral mistake of fact essential to the agreement makes it void; mistake of Indian law does not. Contracts caused by coercion, undue influence, fraud or misrepresentation are voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused.
